name: Cosmopolitanism
summary: Cosmopolitanism holds that all human beings belong to a single moral community, so that national, ethnic or cultural membership does not limit a person's basic moral standing. Its strands range from moral duties of aid and justice that cross borders, to legal and political proposals for global institutions, to a cultural ideal of valuing diversity and exchange. Most adherents favour reformed global governance or a federation of states rather than a world state, and many accept some limited special loyalties.
scope: Mainstream contemporary moral and political cosmopolitanism as presented in the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy and Wikipedia, built on its Stoic origins and on Kant's Perpetual Peace (1795), with later thinkers such as Nussbaum, Appiah, Beitz, Pogge, Held and Archibugi. It excludes the Marxist and economic-liberal strands except where they are noted, and the ethnic 'rootless cosmopolitan' smear. Because the tradition is a philosophy of moral and institutional scope rather than a full program, most domestic economic and cultural questions are inferences marked low confidence.

keyFigures.name: Immanuel Kant
keyFigures.role: Author of Perpetual Peace, which set out cosmopolitan right and a federation of free states.

keyFigures.name: Diogenes of Sinope
keyFigures.role: Ancient Greek philosopher to whom the term 'citizen of the world' is traced.

keyFigures.name: Kwame Anthony Appiah
keyFigures.role: Contemporary philosopher who has written on cosmopolitanism and cultural difference.

sources.title: Cosmopolitanism
sources.author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.usedFor: Varieties of cosmopolitanism and positions on world state, sovereignty, aid, trade, patriotism and culture.

sources.title: Cosmopolitanism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Overview, key figures, and positions on governance, migration, intervention and culture, plus the history of the term as a smear.

sources.title: Perpetual Peace: A Philosophical Essay (trans. M. Campbell Smith)
sources.author: Immanuel Kant
sources.usedFor: Preliminary and definitive articles: republican constitution, federation, standing armies, non-interference, hospitality, criticism of colonial conduct.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a core cosmopolitan topic; the liberal-egalitarian mainstream (Beitz, Pogge, Rawls-style debates in the SEP) extends welfare duties to persons, so domestic provision is inferred as favoured.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from the egalitarian bent of global-justice cosmopolitans; wage floors are not discussed in the sources, and economic cosmopolitans would split.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The SEP records an economic cosmopolitanism (Hegewisch, Hayek, Friedman) favouring global markets, while Marxist and egalitarian cosmopolitans criticise them, so adherents are genuinely split.

public-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; the mainstream is liberal-internationalist and mixed-market, so public ownership is inferred as a mild disagree.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from Singer and Unger's strong duties to aid the distant poor and Pogge's global-justice proposals, which imply redistribution, though no domestic tax rate is stated.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred from the solidarity with workers and the poor typical of global-justice cosmopolitans; the sources do not discuss unions.

property-fundamental.rationale: Cosmopolitan duties of aid and global redistribution (Singer, Unger, Pogge) imply property rights are overridable by claims of the needy; inferred.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The SEP notes critics' worry that multinationals pressure weaker states, and global-justice cosmopolitans favour regulation; inferred rather than central.

cut-welfare.rationale: Cosmopolitans stress duties to the needy of every nation, so cutting welfare runs against core egalitarian concern; inferred.

worker-ownership.rationale: No source ties cosmopolitanism to worker ownership; Marxist and liberal cosmopolitans would split.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from the rights-centred outlook Kant and modern cosmopolitans share, which stresses individual rights against states; terrorism is not discussed.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed by cosmopolitan sources; liberal cosmopolitans lean permissive but there is no stated position.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Cosmopolitans value respect for difference but also free exchange; no source states a position, so adherents split.

strong-leader.rationale: Kant's republican constitution requires separated powers and representation, and cosmopolitans fear despotism, so a gridlock-bypassing leader is disfavoured.

state-harmful.rationale: Cosmopolitans from Kant to Pogge treat states and law as necessary for justice, and Kant wants states to leave the lawless state of nature; the SEP debate is whether states are tools or obstacles, never whether to drop them.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from the pro-peace, anti-violence orientation of Kantian cosmopolitanism; gun ownership is not discussed.

empower-police-military.rationale: Kant's preliminary articles call for abolishing standing armies in time, and cosmopolitans favour reducing militarism.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: No source addresses it; liberal cosmopolitans would lean permissive but others object on equality grounds.

decide-locally.rationale: Cosmopolitans favour authority at global as well as local levels and reject bounded loyalties, though some (Fichte, Pogge) disperse sovereignty across levels; the stress is not on locality.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from the human-rights, equal-dignity outlook; prisons are not discussed.

traditional-family.rationale: Cosmopolitanism treats all human relations as morally wider than kin and nation; inferred disagreement with family as the foundation, no direct source.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from cosmopolitan appeals to universal equal rights; the SEP notes cosmopolitan values invoked for women's emancipation, but marriage is not discussed.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed by cosmopolitan sources; liberal and religious cosmopolitans split.

more-religion-public.rationale: Cosmopolitanism grounds morality in universal reason or shared humanity rather than any one faith; inferred mild disagree.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The SEP reports cosmopolitan values being invoked against slavery, apartheid and colonial exploitation, and Kant condemned European conduct abroad.

gender-social-construct.rationale: No source addresses it, and cosmopolitans range widely.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Cosmopolitans reject strong nationalism and bounded cultural identities (Waldron), though they value cultural attachments within limits.

gradual-change.rationale: Kant favoured gradual reform toward a federation, but cosmopolitan reformers such as Archibugi press for institutional change; no consensus.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Cosmopolitans treat borders as morally weak and poverty-driven migration as world citizenship; Mosterin sees no good reason to restrict movement.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Reformed global governance (Archibugi's World Parliamentary Assembly, Held, Habermas) is a central political-cosmopolitan proposal, though Kant and Beck fear a hegemonic world order.

free-trade.rationale: Economic cosmopolitanism from Smith and Hegewisch favours global free trade, and Kant says commerce works against war; critics within the tradition worry about inequality.

nation-first.rationale: Putting one's own country ahead of global cooperation is the opposite of the moral-cosmopolitan claim that all humans form one moral community; even moderate cosmopolitans accept only limited special duties.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The SEP does not endorse intervention, Kant's non-interference article forbids violent meddling, and Appiah and Mamdani are cited on opposite sides, so adherents are split.

open-borders.rationale: Moral cosmopolitans hold borders morally irrelevant and Mosterin urges free movement, but Kant limits cosmopolitan right to hospitality without settlement and Derrida sees hospitality as conditional.

limit-growth.rationale: No cosmopolitan source takes a position; economic cosmopolitans favour growth and environmentally minded ones do not.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate is a global common problem requiring global duties, inferred from the cosmopolitan emphasis on planet-wide institutions; the sources do not discuss it.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not addressed; no cosmopolitan view on technology as such.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed by the sources and adherents have no shared stance.

revolution-justified.rationale: Kant, the defining modern cosmopolitan, favoured reform and gradual federation over revolution; modern cosmopolitans work through institutions, though Fanon-type figures differ.

experts-over-public.rationale: Cosmopolitans favour democratic structures beyond states (Held, Archibugi, SEP), which implies public voice; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Cosmopolitan economics centres on global markets or egalitarian justice among persons; central planning is not advocated.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not addressed; no source links cosmopolitanism to market socialism.

land-value-tax.rationale: Pogge's global resources dividend is the nearest analogue but is not a land tax; not a cosmopolitan position generally.

tax-inheritance.rationale: No source addresses it; egalitarians lean yes and economic cosmopolitans no.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; global-justice cosmopolitans have discussed it but there is no common view in the sources.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Economic cosmopolitans favour a global free market with minimal state interference; the SEP only notes critics who call protectionism sometimes rational.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Inferred: global-market and liberal-internationalist cosmopolitans do not favour state-led industrial strategy.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Only a Marxist strand would want this, and the mainstream does not; inferred disagree.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Global-governance cosmopolitans favour more, not fewer, coordinating institutions; inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Corporatism is a national-organic model at odds with cosmopolitan universalism; inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: Kant's republican constitution requires representation and separated powers, and cosmopolitans favour democratic structures; single-party guidance contradicts both.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Kant's first definitive article requires a republican constitution, which in his sense excludes despotic monarchy, though he allowed a monarch governing republicanly.

democracy-best.rationale: Cosmopolitan political projects aim at extending democratic voice (Held, Archibugi), though Appiah ties intervention to democracy and does not make the case unconditional.

direct-votes.rationale: Cosmopolitans favour representation in Kant but also participatory global bodies; no stated view.

workers-councils.rationale: Not a cosmopolitan institution; the mainstream favours parliaments and global assemblies; inferred.

right-to-secede.rationale: The SEP says cosmopolitans are wary of unconditional self-determination, yet Mosterin imagines small autonomous polities; no consistent position.

natural-rulers.rationale: Moral cosmopolitanism affirms equal moral standing and opposed feudal hierarchy and colonial rank, so natural rulers are rejected.

political-violence-never.rationale: Kant condemns war and aggression, but the SEP gives no pacifist rule and Fanon-type cosmopolitans accept some violence; adherents split.

war-builds-character.rationale: Kant argues war is a lawless condition to be ended and that commerce cannot coexist with war, and the cosmopolitan tradition centres on peace.

separate-church-state.rationale: Cosmopolitan grounding in universal reason implies a secular public order, but the sources do not address it directly.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Inferred from reliance on universal reason rather than any one tradition's scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Cosmopolitans want public international and cosmopolitan law (Kant, ICC) rather than private provision of defense and justice.

military-superiority.rationale: Seeking superiority over rivals runs against cosmopolitan peace aims and Kant's call to abolish standing armies in time.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Cosmopolitanism holds that all humans belong to one community and rejects bounded cultural identities, so ethnic homogeneity as a goal is rejected.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Only the Marxist strand adopts this; the mainstream liberal and Kantian strands see history as moving toward law and peace.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Egalitarian cosmopolitans such as Beitz and Pogge go beyond opportunity, but the sources do not give a general outcome view.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Cosmopolitans criticise colonial dispossession (Kant) yet are wary of strong rights to culture (Kymlicka and others); no stated position.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Kant condemned colonial injustice and Pogge argues for global duties, but reparations are not specifically addressed.

civilizational-union.rationale: Cosmopolitans look to world-wide rather than civilizational blocs; inferred from the universal community claim.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Moral cosmopolitanism stresses duties to strangers, so self-interest as such is not endorsed, though economic cosmopolitans lean on markets.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Cosmopolitanism is rights-centred: Kant's cosmopolitan law gives individuals rights as citizens of the earth, and human rights are central.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Cosmopolitans point to global exchange as beneficial, so this is an inferred disagree.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Cosmopolitan projects seek democratic voice for individuals, so handing decisions to algorithms is inferred as disfavoured.

restore-past-order.rationale: Cosmopolitanism looks forward to wider community and rejects nostalgic closure around nation or tradition.

direct-action.rationale: Cosmopolitans mainly pursue institutional and legal reform, such as the ICC and global assemblies; inferred.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not addressed by the cosmopolitan sources; no shared stance among adherents.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Kant bars violent interference in other states, but the sources do not endorse an absolute rule against force, and cosmopolitans accept some enforcement through global law.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Economic cosmopolitans favour open markets and the sources do not address price controls; inferred mild disagree.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Nothing in cosmopolitanism supports it, and its commerce and cultural exchange themes oppose it.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Only Marxist/utopian strands propose it; the mainstream favours exchange across borders.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Strong aid duties (Singer, Unger) resemble need-based claims, but cosmopolitans do not endorse a general distribution rule.

production-for-use.rationale: Not addressed; strands split between market and socialist views.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Only the Marxist cosmopolitan strand holds this; the SEP notes Marx's critique of free trade, but the mainstream does not.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Incompatible with Kant's republican constitution and cosmopolitan rights.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Kant holds that the commercial spirit cannot coexist with war, the opposite of this claim.

taxation-theft.rationale: Strong aid and global-justice duties are incompatible with calling taxation theft; inferred.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Moral cosmopolitanism treats individuals as the ultimate units of concern, and cosmopolitan critics fault Rawls for centering peoples; yet cultural-rights views vary.

conscription.rationale: Kant opposed standing armies in time, but allowed voluntary citizen militias for defence; conscription is inferred disfavoured.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Cosmopolitans stress both democratic voice and free movement, but they would not place exit above voting.

state-as-business.rationale: Inferred: citizens are rights-holders, not customers, in cosmopolitan thought.

positive-liberty.rationale: Global-justice cosmopolitans stress the means to act as a matter of justice for the poor; inferred.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not a cosmopolitan claim; in practice it is associated with critics of cosmopolitan elites.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Cosmopolitanism rests on equal moral worth, and the SEP treats racist views among its thinkers as failures to be cosmopolitan.

organic-representation.rationale: Cosmopolitans favour individual and global representation over corporative bodies; inferred.

total-state.rationale: Contradicts Kant's republican constitution and the rights-based cosmopolitan outlook.

national-rebirth.rationale: Cosmopolitanism rejects strong nationalism, so national rebirth as a goal is rejected.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Kant condemned European conquest and states acquiring others' lands, and cosmopolitanism rejects aggressive national aims.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Incompatible with republican law and universal rights.

bound-labor.rationale: Cosmopolitan values have been invoked against slavery and feudal hierarchy, and Kant criticised the slavery of the Sugar Islands.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Kantian cosmopolitanism grounds morality in universal reason; this relativist claim is inferred as opposed, though critical cosmopolitans (Gilroy) may sympathise.

universal-morality.rationale: The core of moral cosmopolitanism: Kant grounds it in universal reason and all humans fall under the same standards.

single-common-good.rationale: Cosmopolitans seek a common human community but accept pluralism of goods (Appiah); adherents split.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: No cosmopolitan source addresses it; cosmopolitans are wary of unconditional national self-determination but split on this case.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Inferred from the weak status cosmopolitans give to ethnic and national ties.

revive-national-language.rationale: Inferred from scepticism toward bounded cultural identities; language revival is not discussed.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Kant opposed war debts only, and no source takes a general view.

economic-freedom.rationale: Economic cosmopolitans agree, egalitarian cosmopolitans do not, so adherents are split.

rule-by-example.rationale: Kant requires rule by law and republican institutions, so government by rulers' example alone is inferred as rejected.

national-self-determination.rationale: The SEP says cosmopolitans are wary of unconditional national self-determination, favouring individuals' democratic control through global institutions.

force-without-un.rationale: Cosmopolitans favour strengthening international institutions and Kant bars violent interference in other states, so unilateral force is disfavoured.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Kantian and Stoic cosmopolitanism grounds universal morality in reason, but modern cosmopolitans, including religious ones, vary.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Strict cosmopolitans hold that aid duties do not weaken with nationality; moderate ones allow some special duties.

class-collaboration.rationale: Not addressed; strands split by economic view.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Cosmopolitans value cultural diversity and exchange, so sacrificing heritage is inferred as disfavoured.

dominated-front.rationale: Cosmopolitanism seeks worldwide cooperation, not bloc fronts, though Fanon's critique of global capital cuts the other way.

workers-nation.rationale: Cosmopolitans reject nationally bounded loyalties; this is inferred from the universal community claim.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The SEP records cosmopolitan values being used for women's emancipation and the equal-worth claim opposes legal role distinctions.

ban-interest.rationale: Economic cosmopolitans favour global markets; interest bans are not a cosmopolitan position.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Cosmopolitan values have been invoked against apartheid, and equal moral worth is central.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Only the Marxist cosmopolitan strand holds this; mainstream cosmopolitans see states as potential tools of justice.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred from global concern over climate; the sources do not address it.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Cosmopolitans value diversity and cultural mixing and reject bounded cultural identities, so demanded assimilation is disfavoured.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy claim, and historically a charge made against cosmopolitans, not a cosmopolitan position; Wikipedia notes the term has been used as a weapon against supposedly rootless groups.

national-mission.rationale: Cosmopolitans reject national exceptionalism, and Kant forbids forcing a constitution on another state.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Cosmopolitan values have been invoked for women's emancipation, but the structural claim itself is inferred.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Conflicts directly with equal moral worth of all persons.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The SEP presents the ICC as a cosmopolitan development holding individuals accountable despite state sovereignty.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Cosmopolitan global-justice duties imply more than a minimal state; economic cosmopolitans such as Hayek-types differ.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Opposed by equal moral worth and the cosmopolitan welcome of cultural mixing.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The foundational claim of moral cosmopolitanism: every human belongs to one moral community and has equal standing.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Kant's republican constitution and cosmopolitan democracy rest on representative consent.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Kant condemned colonial conduct, but the SEP does not classify settler states; no stated position.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Only relevant to the Marxist strand; no stated position for the mainstream.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Equal rights before the law regardless of group is inferred from universal equal rights, though some cosmopolitans value cultural-legal pluralism.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Conflicts with the freedom of conscience and universal rights cosmopolitans uphold.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from opposition to imposing one community's religious norms by law.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Inferred from the cosmopolitan aim to reduce militarism and reject state strengthening for its own sake.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist export surpluses run against the economic-cosmopolitan view of open exchange benefiting all.

population-transfer.rationale: Violates the equal rights of persons that cosmopolitan law protects, and Kant treats peoples as persons, not property.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Cosmopolitanism envisions cooperation among peoples, and Kant sees commerce and law, not struggle between peoples, as leading to peace.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed; liberal cosmopolitans split between militant democracy and free association.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Kant's republicanism and Pogge's concern with global institutional domination suggest agreement, but cosmopolitan sources do not use the phrase.

separated-powers.rationale: Kant's first definitive article requires republican government with separated legislative and executive powers.

vanguard-party.rationale: A disciplined leading party is contrary to the republican and democratic commitments of mainstream cosmopolitanism.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Strict cosmopolitans (Singer, Unger) argue for strong duties to the distant poor.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Cosmopolitan justice theorists (Pogge) blame global institutions for poverty; inferred.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Cosmopolitans encourage a multicultural mix and the peaceful coexistence of traditions.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Cosmopolitans' rights focus makes suspension of legal protections unlikely to be endorsed; inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: Inconsistent with free exchange of ideas that cosmopolitans value (Mosterin, Vazha-Pshavela).

party-commands-army.rationale: Contradicts Kant's republican separation of powers.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from the weak moral status of borders and support for migration.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Cosmopolitan political projects propose layered or federated sovereignty, and Kant's federation of states is a model, though a fully world state is rare.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Kant's republic separates legislative and executive; the presidential claim is inferred as disfavoured.

clerical-rule.rationale: Incompatible with republican constitution and universal reason.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Only the Marxist strand (internationalist) holds this; others would not.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Inferred from cosmopolitan valuing of free cultural exchange.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred from republican limits on power in Kant.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Cosmopolitans favour collective global security but may dislike military blocs; not stated.

people-in-arms.rationale: Kant allowed citizen militias for defence while abolishing standing armies, but general citizen armament is not a cosmopolitan aim.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Cosmopolitanism is historically a cosmopolis, urban cultural outlook; inferred.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Inferred from lower weight given to national self-determination.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Inferred; the claim is common among critics of cosmopolitan elites.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Cosmopolitans value cultural diversity and reject ranking of traditions, though Appiah-style universalists reject full relativism.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred from the rights-centred human-rights orientation, not addressed directly.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from commitments to women's emancipation and universal education.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from the reliance on universal reason.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Cosmopolitans see ancestry as morally arbitrary and favour inclusive citizenship.

minority-language-support.rationale: Cosmopolitans value diversity (Mosterin defends cultural freedoms of language), but the SEP is wary of strong cultural rights.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Cosmopolitans value respect for difference but also equal law; split.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Gilroy's estrangement idea hints at sympathy but is individual.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Moral cosmopolitanism holds that distance and nationality do not weaken duties to the distant needy; this is the core of its global-justice strand.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Global-justice cosmopolitans such as Pogge argue that poor countries bear burdens from an unjust international order, supporting debt relief; inferred from the SEP's account, with economic cosmopolitans split.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Cosmopolitanism takes no stance on national independence versus economic transformation; inferred from its focus on individuals' moral standing.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Kant's republican constitution rests on citizen consent and cosmopolitan democrats favour democratic constitution-making; inferred since it is a domestic procedural question.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Cosmopolitanism grounds moral standing in equal individual worth and rights, and Kant's republican constitution requires freedom; trading freedoms away is rejected.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Kant's Perpetual Peace calls for abolishing standing armies and cosmopolitans favour global institutions over national armament; nuclear weapons are inferred as disfavoured.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Mode of choosing a head of state is not a cosmopolitan question; Kant requires a republican constitution without specifying this.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Not addressed; economic cosmopolitans may favour it while egalitarian ones are sceptical.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Cosmopolitans reject sacred national homelands and favour peace settlements over territorial claims, so land may be traded; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Egalitarian global-justice cosmopolitans treat resources as subject to claims of all persons; economic-liberal cosmopolitans would dissent.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The classification of the USSR is outside cosmopolitanism's scope.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred from cosmopolitan concern for global and future persons, which supports protective action on transnational risks such as climate.

collective-defense.rationale: Cosmopolitans favour collective security and international cooperation over unilateral action, so mutual defense obligations fit; inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Kant forbids one state being acquired by another without consent in the Preliminary Articles of Perpetual Peace, and treats peoples as not property.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Not a cosmopolitan topic; adherents split between secularists and those who value religious pluralism.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; cosmopolitans of both republican and monarchical settings exist.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Cosmopolitanism puts individuals before states, so territorial integrity by force carries little weight; inferred, though Kant also warns against outside interference in a state.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Inferred from cosmopolitan support for layered sovereignty and federal arrangements below and above the state.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Kant argues for a republican constitution on equal citizenship; a sacred ruler of divine descent conflicts with equal moral standing. Inferred.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Domestic tax design is not addressed; adherents are split.

character-from-environment.rationale: Not addressed; cosmopolitan universalism stresses shared human nature while education is valued, so adherents split.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Kant requires a republican constitution under laws that bind the ruler and separate executive from legislative power.

space-expansion.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split between valuing humanity as a whole beyond Earth and prioritising global poverty.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Kant favours a republican constitution with separated powers and distinguishes republican from despotic rule; a stated mixed regime is not his model. Inferred.

leader-cult.rationale: Kant stresses republican equality and the civil constitution; glorifying a leader as the nation embodies nationalist particularism. Inferred.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Not a cosmopolitan concern; the liberal and Kantian mainstream favours cooperation and reform of institutions over class conflict.

land-redistribution.rationale: Egalitarian global-justice cosmopolitans might favour it, while liberal cosmopolitans stress property rights; the tradition does not settle it.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred from moral concern for displaced persons and Kant's hospitality; cosmopolitans also stress freedom of movement, so a right of return is only mildly favoured.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Cosmopolitanism denies that national membership confers special claims, and Kant rejects acquiring states by force or inheritance, so territory by nationality is rejected.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Equal moral standing and individual liberty of conscience for all persons make legal punishment for leaving a religion incompatible.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred from the universal equal standing and freedom of individuals; cosmopolitans oppose state coercion of dress.

common-currency.rationale: Inferred: cosmopolitans favour supranational integration, like the EU, though the sources do not treat currency directly.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Cosmopolitanism favours unity of all humanity over ancestry-based blocs, so union by shared language and descent is inferred as disfavoured.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Cosmopolitans value cultural diversity and minority protection, but some prefer individual rights and mixing to separate institutions; adherents are split.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred from equal rights for all persons wherever they live, though cosmopolitans also defend the freedom to emigrate, so the answer is mild.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Kant and the moral cosmopolitan tradition give weight to moral insight and ideas, so a mainly materialist account is inferred as disfavoured.

ban-cartels.rationale: Not addressed; economic cosmopolitans favour open competition while others favour global regulation; the tradition does not settle it.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not addressed; cosmopolitans split between market-liberal and egalitarian strands.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Cosmopolitan law holds that individual rights bind states and can override sovereignty, so institutions should constrain national majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from equal moral standing and the egalitarian bent of global-justice cosmopolitans; the sources do not discuss quotas.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Kant's hospitality and the free commerce linking nations, along with cosmopolitan openness, run against a closed economic bloc and colonial empires.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred: global-justice cosmopolitans favour fair rules for global trade, though the sources do not state this directly.

moral-incentives.rationale: Not addressed by the tradition; Stoic and Kantian duty fits it, but cosmopolitans do not call for replacing material incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Kant rejects violent revolution and war-making meddling in other states, so insurrectionary armed groups are rejected.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Kant's republican constitution rests on the equality of citizens, and cosmopolitanism denies birth-based moral rank, so abolishing hereditary privilege is favoured.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred from the cosmopolitan ideal of educating pupils as world citizens (Nussbaum in the SEP); a nation-centred curriculum sits uneasily with it, though some would accept it as a starting point.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Kant condemns the conduct of European colonial powers and bases hospitality on equal standing, so rule over "lesser" peoples for their benefit is rejected.

patriotic-education.rationale: The SEP presents cosmopolitans such as Nussbaum as critical of education in patriotic pride, favouring loyalty to humanity first.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not addressed by the tradition; egalitarian cosmopolitans and universalist critics of group classification would split.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary mechanics are not a cosmopolitan topic; no stated position, so adherents are treated as split.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The tradition does not address capitalism's crises; economic-liberal and global-justice cosmopolitans would disagree.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred from opposition to domination of other peoples and from equal moral standing; a state cultivating influence over former colonies runs against this.

delink-world-market.rationale: Global-justice cosmopolitans (Beitz, Pogge) seek fairer global institutions and rules rather than withdrawal from the world economy.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Pogge-style cosmopolitans say the rich benefit from an unjust global order, but the tradition has no position on the claim that rich-country workers are mostly unexploited.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Equal moral standing of all persons makes discrimination on arbitrary grounds hard to defend, though liberal cosmopolitans value freedom of association.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Legal cosmopolitanism centres on universal human rights and Kant favours a republican constitution; entrenchment is inferred, not stated.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Equal moral standing of peoples supports self-determination against imposed borders; inferred.

elective-rulers.rationale: Kant's Perpetual Peace requires republican constitutions with representative government.

minority-veto.rationale: Institutional cosmopolitanism favours collective decision procedures; inferred.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Kant denied a right of rebellion while others allow resistance; split.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Perpetual Peace favours representative government; inferred.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Extension of moral concern beyond one community (Nussbaum) is often applied to animals; inferred.

animal-use-humane.rationale: The ideology's core texts and sources do not address this question, so it is inferred as neutral.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Moral cosmopolitanism holds that the well-off have duties toward the worse off, including across borders.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Stoic cosmopolitanism stressed duty and engagement in public life; inferred.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The ideology's core texts and sources do not address this question, so it is inferred as neutral.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The ideology's core texts and sources do not address this question, so it is inferred as neutral.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Global-justice cosmopolitans such as Pogge argue that the global order disadvantages poor countries; inferred.

native-born-offices.rationale: Cosmopolitanism holds that national origin does not limit a person's basic moral standing.

party-own-road.rationale: The ideology's core texts and sources do not address this question, so it is inferred as neutral.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Cosmopolitanism asserts duties of aid and justice across borders, against going without foreign help.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Territorial claims based on national grievance conflict with cosmopolitan priorities; inferred.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Equal moral standing of persons opposes hereditary political privilege; inferred.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Universalist opposition to ethnic supremacy; inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The ideology's core texts and sources do not address this question, so it is inferred as neutral.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Universal human equality implies slavery was central; inferred.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The ideology's core texts and sources do not address this question, so it is inferred as neutral.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Equal moral concern for all persons; inferred.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Equal moral concern for all persons; inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Universal moral standing implies shared standards; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Perpetual Peace calls for abolishing standing armies and subordinating force to civil law.

paid-care-work.rationale: The ideology's core texts and sources do not address this question, so it is inferred as neutral.

filial-duty.rationale: Not a cosmopolitan topic; family obligations are a particular loyalty the SEP says many cosmopolitans accept in limited form.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred as outside cosmopolitanism's scope; no stated position.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The SEP describes cosmopolitan support for open trade and exchange, so blocking foreign buyers is inferred as disfavoured.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from the stress on individual moral standing and liberty.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition's institutional proposals concern global governance, not domestic mandate.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Not a cosmopolitan topic; inferred as indifferent.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Not addressed; inferred as no settled view.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Kant's republican constitution rests on representative government, from which parliamentary budget control is inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Cultural cosmopolitanism values diversity and exchange, so coercive monolingualism is inferred as disfavoured.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Equal moral standing regardless of nationality is inferred to oppose barring foreigners from land ownership.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split on how to treat unequal outcomes.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Not addressed; inferred as no settled view.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Kant's preliminary articles bar interference in other states' constitution and government by force.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Kant's non-interference article forbids forcible meddling in another state's constitution.

corporate-influence.rationale: Not a core topic; global-justice cosmopolitans criticise concentrated power over political institutions, so this is inferred.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Cosmopolitans favour open exchange across borders; sovereignty-based screening of foreign money is inferred as disfavoured.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Cosmopolitans generally favour open migration, so relying on natalist incentives rather than immigration is inferred as disfavoured.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from the cosmopolitan objection to membership-based exclusion; the sources do not address local property rules.

job-guarantee.rationale: Not addressed by the tradition; egalitarian cosmopolitans might favour it and market-oriented ones would not.

democratic-peace.rationale: Kant's first definitive article ties perpetual peace to republican constitutions and a federation of free states.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Kant demands obedience to law while global-justice cosmopolitans put moral standing above national law; adherents are split.

non-intervention.rationale: Mainstream cosmopolitans accept intervention for grave human-rights abuses and see sovereignty as conditional, though Kant's preliminary articles bar interference.

industrial-unions.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no cosmopolitan line on union structure.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The Wikipedia entry records the 'rootless cosmopolitan' smear that cosmopolitanism is defined against, and universal moral standing rules out such claims.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents have no settled view on legal marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Kant's appendix to Perpetual Peace makes publicity the test of right action by public authority, from which access to government information is inferred.

local-production.rationale: Cosmopolitans favour trade and exchange across borders, so a norm of local production is inferred as disfavoured.

informal-organisation.rationale: Cosmopolitan political projects work through formal institutions and federations; informal small-group organising is inferred as disfavoured.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Cosmopolitans such as Held and Archibugi propose international courts and institutions that can override state sovereignty.

religious-nation.rationale: Cosmopolitan moral community rests on shared humanity, not membership in a national or religious group.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Kant's federation is of free states dealing as equals under law, and cosmopolitan right opposes hierarchy among peoples.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from the global-justice strands (Beitz, Pogge), which favour sharing resources by need over keeping them within a unit.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The tradition does not address the personal/productive property line; strands split between market and egalitarian economics.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred from Kant's non-interference and peace-federation principles, which favour coexistence over campaigns against a system.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Not a cosmopolitan topic; inferred as split because strands divide between market and egalitarian economics.

religion-illusion.rationale: Inferred from the pluralist, tolerant outlook of modern cosmopolitans, who generally do not treat religion as an illusion to be outgrown.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Strands diverge on market versus egalitarian economics, so adherents are split.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not addressed; liberal-egalitarian cosmopolitans lean to legal reform while others favour structural change, so split.

socialized-care.rationale: Not addressed; inferred as split across the egalitarian and market strands.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The cultural strand values exchange, hybridity and diversity, which is opposed to purging foreign words.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on lawful commitments and respect for peoples' standing, which favours keeping agreements.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred: cosmopolitanism favours broad universal institutions over small closed communities.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the equal moral standing of all persons and hospitality ideals, which oppose steering settlement to bind minorities.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Cosmopolitanism is a moral and institutional philosophy, not an economic system; adherents come from both camps.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Equal moral standing of persons regardless of membership implies that historical ties give no stronger claim over current residents; inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; inferred from the universal moral standing of every person.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from equal moral standing and universal human rights.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Kant's republican constitution and rights-respecting order, which cosmopolitanism builds on, rule out suppressing opposition; inferred.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred from the liberal commitment to freedom of conscience and equal standing of persons.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Perpetual Peace condemns European colonial conduct toward other peoples as a breach of the right of hospitality.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred that cosmopolitanism is not an ideology of religious armed duty.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred from its commitment to peaceful, rights-based global order.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Not a core topic; inferred from the emphasis on persons as the units of moral concern.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Not a core topic; inferred from the equal-standing principle applied to all forms of discrimination.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the equal moral standing of all persons.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; the liberal mainstream of the tradition tends to respect individual autonomy at life's end.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The tradition is a moral philosophy that spans left and right positions on economics, so adherents are split.

alienated-labor.rationale: The Marxist strand is excluded from the audited scope, and mainstream cosmopolitans do not take a position; inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred from valuing cultural diversity and equal standing across cultures.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Inferred: cosmopolitan authority is grounded in human beings' equal standing, not in God.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred from the liberal tolerance of diversity of practice.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not a core topic; inferred from the liberal-egalitarian mainstream.

social-market-economy.rationale: Not a core topic; inferred from the liberal-egalitarian mainstream.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Perpetual Peace, Preliminary Article 3, says standing armies shall in time be abolished entirely.

rich-first.rationale: Global-justice cosmopolitans (Beitz, Pogge) hold that persons everywhere have equal claims, which cuts against letting some grow rich first; inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Cosmopolitans favour global institutions, but the tradition splits on blocs and alliances.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Kant's Perpetual Peace requires a republican constitution, which sits ill with hereditary rule as a principle of office.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Not a cosmopolitan topic; adherents hold a range of views on credit and banking.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Pogge-style critics of the global order favour it, but many cosmopolitans accept conditionality and aid by institutions; inferred split.

property-franchise.rationale: Equal moral standing of every person is the core claim, which excludes wealth-qualified voting.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Cosmopolitan universalism extends equal regard to all persons and is compatible with ecofeminist concern; inferred.

reification.rationale: The liberal mainstream treats markets as compatible with equal moral standing; inferred, as the sources do not discuss reification.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Cosmopolitans value free expression but the sources do not address media ownership; adherents split.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Kant's republican constitution and definitive articles rest on public law applied by regular institutions rather than arbitrary rule.

racial-franchise.rationale: Moral standing is not limited by ethnic membership, so ethnic limits on political rights contradict the core claim.

online-participation.rationale: Cosmopolitan democrats such as Held and Archibugi favour wider participation across borders, which online forums extend; inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: Global accountability and transparency of institutions follow from cosmopolitan institutional proposals; inferred.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Restricting marriage by religion makes membership of a community limit personal standing, which cosmopolitanism rejects.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Singling out people by religion contradicts equal moral standing and the hospitality ideal in Kant.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Cosmopolitan democrats such as Held and Archibugi propose deliberative, citizen-based global institutions, so lot-chosen assemblies fit; inferred from that strand, not a core claim.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Kant-style Enlightenment cosmopolitanism prizes reason and openness to other traditions over inherited authority; inferred, as the sources do not address religious reform.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Global-justice cosmopolitans such as Beitz and Pogge criticise extreme material inequality, but the link to political liberty is inferred rather than central.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Equal moral standing regardless of group membership implies that sexual orientation should not bar service; inferred from the universal moral-community principle.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Respect for each person's moral standing and cultural diversity implies state neutrality rather than imposed unbelief; inferred.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Cosmopolitanism concerns moral scope and institutions rather than criminal justice; most adherents back reformed legal institutions, as in international courts.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Cosmopolitan democracy proposals stress representation of all affected people, but the literature has no settled view on communal power-sharing; adherents are split.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Cosmopolitans tend to see aid as a duty of justice carried out through institutions, not left to private charity; inferred from the aid duties discussed.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits are a domestic institutional question the tradition does not address.

vote-delegation.rationale: Cosmopolitan democracy supports wider participation, but delegable voting is not discussed and the literature does not settle it.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Concern for all of humanity, including future generations, supports priority for catastrophic risks; inferred from the single moral community principle.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Equal moral standing of all persons implies equal eligibility regardless of sex; inferred.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Equal moral standing of persons implies equality within marriage; inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Equal moral standing for all persons suggests residents should have a political voice wherever they live; inferred, as the tradition rarely addresses local franchise.

rent-control.rationale: Housing policy is not addressed by cosmopolitan theory and adherents hold varied economic views.

abolish-ip.rationale: Cosmopolitans split between valuing the free flow of ideas and worrying about global access to medicines under patents; no settled position.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Drilled national-service youth movements run against the ideal of loyalty to humanity over the nation; inferred from the anti-nationalist core.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Kant's Perpetual Peace calls for ending the arms race and standing armies, so a cosmopolitan leans against basing nuclear weapons; inferred.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Kant bars interference in other states, but foreign bases under collective arrangements are not addressed and adherents differ.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Cosmopolitan concern for human rights and international criminal law supports recognising atrocities against any people; inferred.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Global-justice cosmopolitans such as Pogge and Beitz stress that unearned advantage from ownership or birth should not set life chances; inferred.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Most cosmopolitans, Kant included, accept self-defence and defence of others, and support enforcing human rights by force in some cases; inferred.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Cosmopolitanism treats national identity as contingent and cultures as mixed and changing, rejecting essentialist continuity; inferred from the anti-parochial core.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The tradition takes no position on the metaphysics of sex.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between universal categories of humanity and attention to difference.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Honouring those who die for the nation as saints runs against loyalty to humanity over the nation; inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Kantian and Stoic cosmopolitanism rests on reason and universal moral law rather than a cosmic struggle of good and evil; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Diaspora and homeland relations are not addressed; cosmopolitans value cultural exchange but are indifferent to nation-building.

culture-before-state.rationale: Cosmopolitanism does not treat national cultural renewal as a priority and favours universal institutions; inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: The tradition is secular or religiously plural and says nothing on this.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Nussbaum's capabilities approach values the dignity of all persons, but the tradition has no settled view on judging religious texts.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Equal moral standing regardless of ethnicity or nationality excludes reserving economic life for a national majority; Kant's universal hospitality points the same way.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Cosmopolitans favour federation and shared institutions over carving territory into single-people units; inferred.

independent-unions.rationale: Not a cosmopolitan topic; the tradition concerns moral scope rather than domestic labour organisation.

municipal-property.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; cosmopolitanism has no stance on forms of ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from Kant's federation of free states and the SEP's global-institution proposals, which favour coordination that leaves members self-governing.

family-wage.rationale: A domestic economic question the tradition does not address.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed; cosmopolitan concern with global health does not decide regulatory speed.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Cosmopolitans might prefer funding aimed at the global poor, but the sources give no view on ageing research.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not a cosmopolitan topic, and adherents might weigh privacy against global enforcement.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition has no stated view.

person-over-state.rationale: The SEP presents individuals as the ultimate units of moral concern, and Kant's formula of treating persons as ends rather than means underlies the tradition, so state or community aims cannot override a person's standing.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Stoic origins include a rational and divine element, but modern cosmopolitans are religious and secular alike.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Not addressed; cosmopolitan federalism concerns powers between states and global bodies.

dense-cities.rationale: Not a cosmopolitan topic, though the cultural strand values urban exchange; the sources do not settle it.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The SEP defines cosmopolitanism as moral standing that national, ethnic or cultural membership does not limit, so organising around racial interests runs against its core claim.

racial-pride.rationale: Cosmopolitans treat ancestry as morally arbitrary and value diversity, so pride in race is not a legitimate basis for them, though a mild ancestral pride is tolerated.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Kant's Perpetual Peace argues against wars of aggression and standing armies, though modern cosmopolitans debate humanitarian intervention.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Cosmopolitans give moral standing to persons, not to language-defined nations; inferred from the SEP's account of its universalism, and a shared language is not treated as a basis for political unity.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from the universalist premise that all citizens are equal members of one political community; separate religious electorates are not discussed.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred: cosmopolitans see other states as partners in shared institutions rather than plotters, but the topic is not addressed.

free-public-college.rationale: Not a core topic; inferred from the egalitarian cosmopolitan view that opportunity should not depend on wealth.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Not a core topic; global-justice cosmopolitans such as Pogge propose resource and emission levies, so pricing pollution is inferred as favoured.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the universal moral concern that includes all persons, which cosmopolitans extend across generations; the SEP entry does not centre it.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The tradition's universalism is gender-neutral and does not endorse or reject a distinct women's outlook; adherents are split.

arms-reduction.rationale: Kant's Perpetual Peace holds that standing armies shall in time be totally abolished, and cosmopolitans broadly support multilateral arms limits.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Kant's Perpetual Peace rejects treaties with secretly reserved matter and makes publicity the test of right; cosmopolitans carry this to open international law.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from cosmopolitan support for open exchange across borders, though global-justice strands favour regulating finance; adherents differ.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Kant wants standing armies abolished and states bound by law, but cosmopolitanism sets no view on domestic arms monopolies; inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Kant condemns war and the Stoic tradition puts humanity above the state, but the sources opened do not endorse refusal of orders and adherents split on just war.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Not a core topic; inferred from the egalitarian bent of mainstream cosmopolitans.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from the egalitarian bent of mainstream global-justice cosmopolitans; not discussed in the sources.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Not addressed by the tradition; economic cosmopolitans and egalitarians would split.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Global-justice cosmopolitans such as Beitz and Pogge argue that the global economic order should be reformed to serve the world's poor.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no mainstream cosmopolitan position.

sacred-nation.rationale: Cosmopolitanism denies that national membership limits moral standing and treats the nation as at most a limited special loyalty, not a sacred one.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not addressed; egalitarians might favor it and others would not.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Global-justice cosmopolitans focus on cross-border inequality; the sources do not address regions within a state.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Cosmopolitanism rests on the equal moral worth of every human being as a shared basis for rights; the sources do not address redesigning human nature.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from the liberal tradition's support for open communication and cultural exchange; not stated in the sources.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Stoic and Kantian cosmopolitanism is about shared moral community, not religious truth; Appiah-style cosmopolitans accept pluralism. Inferred.

farm-price-support.rationale: Cosmopolitanism concerns cross-border justice, not agricultural policy; adherents split on trade protection.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Kant's Perpetual Peace argues for ending standing armies and building a federation of states for peace, so cosmopolitans lean toward disarmament; inferred, adherents differ on unilateral steps.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Cosmopolitans split between strict liability, global environmental regulation and other tools; the sources do not settle it.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Cosmopolitans favor universal legal norms and global institutions over local customary authority; inferred.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Cosmopolitanism has no position on sentencing; adherents split.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred: cosmopolitans stress inclusion and equal standing of persons and would worry about barriers to participation; the sources do not discuss voter ID.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred: cosmopolitans value cross-border exchange and communication and would oppose cutting it off; the sources do not mention shutdowns.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed; cosmopolitans support welfare duties but do not share a view on the form of domestic benefits.

women-suffrage.rationale: Equal moral standing of all persons is the core cosmopolitan premise, which entails equal political rights for women; inferred from that principle.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred: cosmopolitans value cultural diversity and are split on whether religion is a major cause of women's oppression.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from global-justice cosmopolitans (Beitz, Pogge) who treat natural resources as a shared global stake, not owned by whoever claims them first.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: The SEP presents international criminal law as an extension of Kant's cosmopolitan right, holding individuals answerable beyond state sovereignty.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's Stoic and Kantian grounding in universal reason, which does not rest on any one scripture.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the universal equal moral standing of every individual, which would extend to women inside group self-rule.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from cosmopolitan democrats such as Held and Archibugi, who want representation to reach people directly, not through layers of delegates.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from the equal moral standing of all persons and the rejection of membership-based privilege.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from the cultural strand's valuing of diversity and from the limited-special-loyalties position, which allows group self-rule.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from the ideal that persons, not states, are the basic units of moral concern, so residents' choice carries weight.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Adherents split: borders are seen as morally arbitrary, but a peaceful federation of existing states also favours stable frontiers.

simple-living.rationale: The sources do not address it; Stoic austerity pulls one way and the strand valuing cultural exchange and abundance pulls the other.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred; open movement of people favours free settlement, while the diversity strand supports protecting indigenous cultures.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from the equal moral standing of all persons, which implies treating women and men alike in any shared civic burden.

missingStatements.text: Wealthy countries have a duty to give substantial aid to the world's poor, regardless of where those people live.
missingStatements.rationale: Strict cosmopolitans such as Singer and Unger hold that duties to aid are not weakened by distance or nationality.

missingStatements.text: Individuals who commit grave crimes should be tried before international courts even against their own state's wishes.
missingStatements.rationale: The SEP presents the International Criminal Court as an extension of Kant's cosmopolitan law, holding individuals responsible despite state sovereignty.

notes: Strands diverge on a world state (Cloots, Cabrera for; Kant, Rawls, Beck against), on strict versus moderate special duties to compatriots, and on market versus egalitarian economics. Kant himself limited cosmopolitan right to hospitality without a right to settle.
